title: What If You Were Born as Blackbeard? | The Golden Age of Piracy

paras: If you were born as Blackbeard, you'd become the most feared pirate alive.
You'd hold an entire city hostage. For a box of medicine.
And your head?
Will end up hanging from the front of a navy ship.
But right now?
You're a baby, somewhere on the edge of the Atlantic.
No beard. No ship. Not even a name anyone agrees on.
It's around 1680.
Some say you're born in Bristol, England. Others say Jamaica.
Your last name shows up as Teach, Thatch, Thache, and half a dozen more.
Nobody wrote down your childhood.
Nobody thought they'd need to.
So for now, you're just a boy who can't stop looking at the harbour.
In 1702, England goes to war with France and Spain.
They call it Queen Anne's War.
And England needs more fighting ships than it has.
So the crown hands out papers to private captains.
Attack enemy ships, keep most of the loot, and it's all legal.
They're called privateers.
The story goes that you sail on them, out of Jamaica.
You learn guns, rope, and how fast a merchant ship gives up.
Remember that last part.
Then, in 1713, peace.
Overnight, thousands of trained sea-raiders have no job.
And no plan to become farmers.
They gather on an island in the Bahamas called New Providence.
Its harbour town, Nassau, has no real government.
It becomes a republic of pirates.
Around 1716, you join a captain named Benjamin Hornigold.
He's tough, careful, and he likes you.
He gives you a captured sloop of your own.
Remember Hornigold.
Together you raid ships carrying flour from Havana.
Wine from Madeira. Anything that floats and pays.
Your first report in the records calls you Thatch, with six guns and seventy men.
You're in your thirties now.
Late for a beginner.
Right on time for a legend.
In 1717, you meet the strangest pirate in the Caribbean.
His name is Stede Bonnet.
He's a rich plantation owner from Barbados who simply bought a warship.
He knows nothing about the sea.
His own crew can't stand him.
So you take command of his ship, the Revenge, and keep him aboard as a guest.
He calls it a partnership.
You call it a free ship.
Remember Bonnet.
Meanwhile, Hornigold refuses to attack British ships.
His crew votes him out.
Your teacher sails away. And now the fleet listens to you.
November 1717, near the island of Saint Vincent.
You spot a big French ship, La Concorde.
She's a slave ship, carrying hundreds of captive Africans.
Your two ships fire one broadside each.
The French crew is sick and outgunned.
They surrender.
You make her yours, and mount around forty cannons on her deck.
You give her a new name.
Queen Anne's Revenge.
Now you have a floating fortress and around three hundred men.
You're not a pirate anymore.
You're a navy.
Quick pause.
So many of you asked for a pirate, so here's the real one.
Who should live next? Leave a name in the comments.
And if you want a new life every day, subscribe.
In December 1717, a captured captain describes you.
A tall, thin man, with a very black beard that he wears very long.
From now on, the world calls you Blackbeard.
And you lean into it.
You twist your beard into little braids, tied with ribbons.
Before a fight, you tuck burning fuses under your hat.
Smoke curls around your face.
Three pairs of pistols across your chest.
A cutlass at your hip.
One writer says hell couldn't make a scarier face.
Remember how fast a merchant ship gives up?
You make it faster.
If you look terrifying, nobody fights back.
There's no verified account of you ever harming a prisoner.
Remember that.
Your own men aren't so lucky.
The story goes that one night in your cabin, you blow out the candle and fire two pistols under the table.
Your officer, Israel Hands, takes a ball in the knee.
Your reason? If you don't shoot one now and then, they'll forget who you are.
Remember Israel Hands.
You park your fleet at the mouth of Charleston harbour, South Carolina.
Nothing gets in. Nothing gets out.
For nearly a week, you stop every ship that tries.
One of them carries Samuel Wragg, a member of the colony's council.
You take him and the other passengers hostage.
Your demand surprises everyone.
Not gold.
A chest of medicine.
Send it, or the governor gets the prisoners' heads.
Your messengers go ashore.
Their boat flips on the way. Then they get drunk in town.
You give them two more days.
The medicine arrives.
You let the hostages go, minus their valuables.
Nobody agrees on who on board was sick.
Remember the medicine.
But a whole city just learned your name.
June 1718, Beaufort Inlet, North Carolina.
Queen Anne's Revenge runs straight onto a sandbar.
The mast cracks. She's finished.
Was it an accident?
Your own boatswain later says you did it on purpose.
A fleet that big has too many mouths to share the loot.
So you load the best of the treasure onto a small sloop.
You leave about twenty-five men stranded on a bare sandbank.
And you strip Bonnet's ship and sail off without him.
Remember Bonnet, your guest?
He rescues the stranded men two days later.
He goes back to piracy, gets caught, and is hanged in Charleston.
You never see him again.
Meanwhile, the king is offering pardons to any pirate who quits.
Remember Hornigold?
He takes the pardon, and becomes a pirate hunter.
You take one too.
From Charles Eden, the governor of North Carolina, in the little town of Bath.
One writer says you only did it to wait for a better chance.
You settle in.
The legend says you marry a planter's daughter, your fourteenth wife.
Records suggest you only ever married once.
By August, you're back at sea.
You bring a French ship full of sugar into Bath.
A local official and the governor both get their share.
Everyone's happy. Except the governor next door.
Alexander Spotswood, the governor of Virginia, wants you gone.
North Carolina isn't even his colony.
He sends Lieutenant Robert Maynard anyway, with two small sloops and fifty-seven men.
November 21st, 1718. Ocracoke Inlet.
Maynard finds your sloop, the Adventure, at sunset.
You have maybe twenty-five men. Israel Hands is ashore, in Bath.
At dawn, Maynard moves in.
You shout across the water.
Damnation seize my soul if I give you quarter, or take any from you.
Your broadside tears his sloops apart.
Maynard's men go quiet. The deck looks empty.
So you board.
It's a trap.
Sailors pour up from below.
Maynard fires. His sword snaps against yours.
Then a Scottish sailor swings at your neck.
They count five bullet wounds, and about twenty cuts.
Remember the man who never had to fight?
This time, you fought.
Your head is cut off and hung under the bowsprit.
Your body goes over the side.
Legend says it swims around the ship three times before it sinks.
You're somewhere between thirty-five and forty.
Your pirate career lasted barely two years.
Your surviving crew is tried in Virginia, and most of them hang.
Remember Israel Hands?
He testifies against them, and walks free.
The story goes he ends his days begging in London.
In 1996, divers find Queen Anne's Revenge on the bottom of Beaufort Inlet.
Cannons, anchors, and a ship's doctor's tools.
Remember the medicine?
Part of the legend was smoke. The ship was real.
Your teacher became a pirate hunter.
Your partner hanged.
Your flagship sank on purpose.
You held a city hostage, and asked for medicine.
You built a face so frightening that nobody fought you.
Until one man did.
So tell me.
Was Blackbeard the most dangerous pirate who ever lived, or just the best actor?
